title: Vicini, amici e rapporti
sub: Phrasal verbs e -ing / to - lamentele cortesi e accordi
grammar: Phrasal verbs (separabili e non), gerundio vs infinito con cambio di significato (remember, stop, try)
situation: Vicini di casa: lamentele cortesi e accordi

lessons.title: Phrasal verbs e forme in -ing / to
lessons.intro: Due punti che mettono in difficoltà gli italiani: i phrasal verbs (dove va il pronome?) e i verbi che cambiano significato a seconda che siano seguiti da -ing o da to + verbo.

steps.title: Phrasal verbs: tre famiglie
steps.body:
Un phrasal verb è un verbo + particella (up, off, after...) con un significato proprio. Ce ne sono tre tipi:
- **senza complemento** (intransitivi): She **grew up** in Leeds. / The car **broke down**.
- **separabili**: il complemento può stare in mezzo o dopo: **turn off** the light = turn the light **off**. Se il complemento è un **pronome**, va SEMPRE in mezzo: turn **it** off (mai «turn off it»).
- **non separabili**: il complemento sta sempre dopo: **look after** my sister -> look after **her**. Come: look for, get over, run into, deal with.

Con tre elementi (verbo + 2 particelle) il complemento va in fondo: **put up with** the noise, **look forward to** the weekend, **run out of** milk.
ex: Could you turn the music down, please?
Puoi abbassare la musica, per favore?
I picked it up at the station.
L'ho ritirato alla stazione.
She looks after her grandmother.
Si prende cura della nonna.
table: turn off the TV / turn the TV off

steps.title: Come si studiano e dove sbagliano gli italiani
steps.body:
- Si imparano **a blocchi con un esempio**, non traducendo la particella: «give up» non è «dare su».
- Molti hanno un equivalente più formale: **put off** = postpone, **find out** = discover, **turn down** = refuse (o abbassare).
- Errori tipici: «Turn off it», «I look for him since an hour», «I'm looking forward to see you» (qui **to** è una preposizione: serve -ing), «She takes care to the cat» (-> looks after).
- Nel dubbio sulla posizione, usa il pronome in mezzo: con i separabili è sempre corretto, con i non separabili è sbagliato (non si dice «look her after»). Controlla sul dizionario.
ex: I'm looking forward to meeting your family.
Non vedo l'ora di conoscere la tua famiglia.
We ran out of petrol on the motorway.
Siamo rimasti senza benzina in autostrada.

steps.title: Remember, forget, stop, try: -ing o to?
steps.body:
Alcuni verbi cambiano **significato** secondo la forma che segue:
- **remember / forget + -ing** = ricordare / dimenticare qualcosa **già fatto**: I remember **locking** the door. (ricordo di averla chiusa)
- **remember / forget + to** = ricordare / dimenticare **di fare** qualcosa: Remember **to lock** the door! (non dimenticare di farlo)
- **stop + -ing** = smettere di fare: She stopped **smoking**.
- **stop + to** = fermarsi **per** fare: We stopped **to have** a coffee.
- **try + -ing** = provare per vedere l'effetto: Try **restarting** the computer.
- **try + to** = cercare di (con fatica): I tried **to open** the window, but it was stuck.
- **regret + -ing** = rimpiangere di aver fatto; **regret + to** = dispiacersi di dover (formale): We regret **to inform** you...
ex: I'll never forget meeting her for the first time.
Non dimenticherò mai la prima volta che l'ho incontrata.
Don't forget to post the letter.
Non dimenticare di imbucare la lettera.
We stopped to look at the view.
Ci siamo fermati a guardare il panorama.

steps.title: Ripasso: verbi seguiti da -ing o to
steps.body:
- Solo **-ing**: enjoy, avoid, suggest, mind, finish, keep, practise, give up.
- Solo **to + verbo**: decide, hope, want, plan, promise, manage, refuse, afford.
- Dopo una **preposizione** sempre -ing: interested in learning, good at cooking, before leaving. Anche dopo **to** preposizione: look forward to seeing, get used to living.
- **Used to + base** = un'abitudine passata: I used to live here. **Be/get used to + -ing** = essere abituato a: I'm used to getting up early.

Errori tipici: «She suggested to go», «I enjoy to read», «I'm used to get up early».
ex: She suggested going to the cinema.
Ha proposto di andare al cinema.
He refused to apologise.
Si è rifiutato di scusarsi.

steps.s: It's cold in here. Please ___ the heating.
steps.it: Qui fa freddo. Accendi il riscaldamento, per favore.
steps.why: Accendere = turn on; turn off = spegnere.

steps.s: I'll ___ your children while you're at the dentist.
steps.it: Mi occupo io dei tuoi bambini mentre sei dal dentista.
steps.why: Look after = prendersi cura di; look for = cercare.
Con un pronome il phrasal verb separabile si spezza: turn it off.

steps.q: Completa: «I'm looking forward ___ you next week.»
steps.text: Non vedo l'ora di vederti la settimana prossima.
steps.why: Nel phrasal verb look forward to, «to» è una preposizione: serve -ing.

steps.s: I remember ___ him at Sara's party last year. He was wearing a green hat.
steps.why: Remember + -ing: ricordo qualcosa che è già successo.

steps.s: Remember ___ some milk on your way home, please.
steps.why: Remember + to: non dimenticare di fare qualcosa.

steps.s: We stopped ___ a coffee on the way to the airport.
steps.why: Stop + to = ci siamo fermati per prendere un caffè. Stop + -ing significherebbe smettere.

steps.q: Che cosa significa «I tried to open the window»?
opts: Ho cercato di aprire la finestra (ma forse non ci sono riuscito).
Ho aperto la finestra per vedere che effetto faceva.
Ho smesso di aprire la finestra.
steps.why: Try + to = fare uno sforzo; try + -ing = fare una prova per vedere l'effetto.

steps.q: Completa con la forma giusta di see
steps.s: I'll never forget ___ the sea for the first time.
steps.why: Forget + -ing: un ricordo di qualcosa già fatto.

steps.q: Completa con la forma giusta di lock
steps.s: She forgot ___ the door, so the burglar just walked in.
steps.why: Forget + to: si è dimenticata di farlo.

steps.q: Traduci in inglese (usa put up with)
answers: I can't put up with this noise any more
I can't put up with this noise anymore
I can't put up with the noise any more
I can't put up with the noise anymore
I can't put up with this noise any longer
I can't put up with the noise any longer
steps.why: Put up with = sopportare; è un phrasal verb a tre parti.

steps.s: Please turn off it; it's too loud.
answers: Please turn it off; it's too loud
steps.why: Con un pronome il complemento va in mezzo: turn it off.

steps.s: I look forward to see you next week.
answers: I look forward to seeing you next week
I'm looking forward to seeing you next week
steps.why: Dopo look forward to serve -ing.

steps.s: She suggested to go to the cinema.
answers: She suggested going to the cinema
steps.why: Dopo suggest si usa -ing.

steps.s1: My sister takes care of the baby on Mondays.
steps.s2: My sister ___ the baby on Mondays.
steps.why: Take care of = look after.

steps.s1: I clearly recall that I locked the door.
steps.why: Ricordo di aver fatto: remember + -ing.

steps.it: Ho smesso di fumare due anni fa.
steps.en: I stopped smoking two years ago
steps.why: Smettere di = stop + -ing.

lessons.title: Amici, vicini, rapporti
lessons.intro: Le parole per parlare di relazioni: dalla lite al fare pace, dal perdere i contatti al chiedere un favore. Molte sono phrasal verbs: studiale con l'esempio.

ex: She's not a close friend, just an acquaintance.
Non è un'amica stretta, solo una conoscente.
They had an argument about who should do the washing-up.
Hanno litigato su chi dovesse lavare i piatti.
words.note: Falso amico: «argomento» si dice topic o subject.

ex: He apologised for being late.
Si è scusato per il ritardo.
words.note: Si dice apologise TO someone FOR something. Nome: apology.

ex: It was all a misunderstanding.
Era tutto un malinteso.
They fell out over money.
Hanno litigato per una questione di soldi.
words.note: Si dice fall out WITH someone.

ex: We had a row, but we made up the next day.
Abbiamo litigato, ma abbiamo fatto pace il giorno dopo.
Let's meet for coffee and catch up.
Vediamoci per un caffè e facciamo il punto.
words.note: Catch up WITH someone / ON something.

ex: Promise you'll keep in touch when you move.
Promettimi che resterai in contatto quando ti trasferirai.
I lost touch with most of my school friends.
Ho perso i contatti con la maggior parte degli amici di scuola.
I don't trust people who never listen.
Non mi fido di chi non ascolta mai.
words.note: Si dice trust someone, senza preposizione.

ex: He was jealous of his brother's success.
Era geloso del successo del fratello.
My flatmate always leaves dirty plates in the sink.
Il mio coinquilino lascia sempre i piatti sporchi nel lavandino.
We're having a housewarming on Saturday.
Sabato facciamo la festa per la nuova casa.
Could I ask you a favour?
Posso chiederti un favore?

steps.s: We had a big ___ about money and haven't spoken since.
steps.why: Argument = lite. «Argomento» è topic o subject: falso amico.

steps.s: It was just a ___ : I thought you said Tuesday, not Thursday.
steps.why: Misunderstanding = malinteso.

steps.s: We used to be close, but we ___ touch after he moved to Canada.
steps.why: Si dice lose touch (with someone), non «miss touch».

steps.s: Could you do me a ___ ? Can you pick up my parcel on Friday?
steps.why: Do someone a favour = fare un favore a qualcuno.

steps.s: He sent me a long ___ for missing my birthday.
steps.why: Serve un nome: apologise -> apology (non «apologise»).
Acquaintance = conoscente. Non è «conoscenza» (knowledge).

lessons.title: Il rumore che ha fatto nascere un'amicizia
lessons.intro: Un articolo di rivista sulla vita nel palazzo: dal fastidio per il rumore alla scoperta dei vicini. Cerca come cambia l'atteggiamento della scrittrice.

steps.title: The neighbour upstairs
steps.text:
When I moved into my flat in Leeds two years ago, I didn't know a single person in the building. I remember thinking that big cities were lonely places, and I almost gave up trying to meet anyone. Then the noise started.

The man in the flat above, Greg, played the drums every Tuesday night. I put up with it for a month. I tried wearing earplugs, I tried turning my music up, and I even tried to sleep in the kitchen. Nothing worked. Finally I decided to talk to him, but I was so nervous that I wrote a list of things to say. On Wednesday I knocked on his door, holding the list.

To my surprise, Greg was extremely embarrassed. "I'm so sorry," he said. "I had no idea you could hear me. I forgot to ask the neighbours before I bought the drums." He explained that he had been practising for a concert, and he promised to stop playing after nine o'clock. Then he asked me whether I wanted to come and listen to him play. I said no, but he insisted, and I went upstairs the following Sunday.

That evening changed everything. We talked for hours, and I found out that he had grown up only twenty miles from my home town. A few weeks later he introduced me to Mei, who lives opposite, and to an elderly couple, the Hendersons, who have lived in the building for forty years. Now we have a shared group chat, and we take it in turns to water each other's plants when we're away. Last winter, when I was ill, Mei did my shopping and Mr Henderson sent me a card.

I still think about how close I came to doing nothing. If I hadn't knocked on that door, I would probably still be pretending that nobody lived above me. So my advice is simple: don't wait for the noise to get worse. Be polite, be honest, and try talking to your neighbours. You might be surprised by what you find out.

qs.q: How did the writer feel about the new city at first?
qs.why: «I remember thinking that big cities were lonely places».

qs.q: What did Greg do on Tuesday nights?
Why did the writer write a list?
opts: The writer was nervous about talking to him.
The writer wanted to give it to him.
The writer was afraid of forgetting the date.
qs.why: «I was so nervous that I wrote a list of things to say».

qs.q: How did Greg react when the writer knocked on his door?
Greg promised not to play after ___ .
Greg and the writer grew up in the same town.
qs.why: «grown up only twenty miles from my home town»: vicino, non lo stesso paese.

qs.q: What is the writer's main advice?
opts: Speak politely to neighbours before things get worse.
qs.why: Ultimo paragrafo: «Be polite, be honest, and try talking to your neighbours».

steps.q: Nel testo, «I put up with it for a month» significa:
opts: Per un mese l'ho messo da parte.
steps.why: Put up with = sopportare.

steps.s: They take it in ___ to water the plants.
steps.why: Take it in turns = fare a turno.

steps.q: Completa con una parola dal testo
steps.s: I found ___ that he had grown up near my home town.
steps.why: Find out = scoprire.
Falso amico: embarrassed = in imbarazzo.

lessons.title: Una chiacchierata tra vicini
lessons.intro: Una vicina bussa alla porta per un problema, ma con molto garbo. Ascolta come si chiede e come si trova un accordo senza litigare.

steps.title: A quick word
steps.it: Ascolta la conversazione e rispondi. Puoi riascoltarla e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Oh, hello, Mrs Collins. Is everything all right?
Hello, Dan. Yes, yes, I just wanted a quick word, if you've got a minute.
Of course. Come in. Would you like a cup of tea?
No, thank you, I won't stay long. It's about Biscuit.
Oh dear. Has he done something?
Not exactly. It's just that he barks quite a lot when you're out. Yesterday he barked from nine until about twelve, and I couldn't concentrate on my crossword.
Oh, I'm so sorry. I had no idea. I leave for work at half past eight, and I suppose he gets lonely.
I thought it might be that. I don't want to make a fuss, I love dogs, but it's rather difficult in the mornings.
You're right, and I really appreciate you telling me. I'll try leaving the radio on for him. And I could ask my sister to take him out for a walk at lunchtime.
That would be lovely. Actually, I could pop in myself on Wednesdays, because I'm at home. I wouldn't mind giving him a biscuit.
Really? That's very kind. But I don't want to take advantage.
Not at all. Shall we try it for two weeks and see how it goes?
Deal. Let me give you my mobile number, so you can text me if there's a problem.
Perfect. Thank you, Dan. And remember to bring Biscuit round for tea one day.
I will. Thanks again, Mrs Collins.

opts: The dog barks when Dan is out.

qs.q: Yesterday the dog barked until about ___ .
What time does Dan leave for work?
What does Mrs Collins offer to do on Wednesdays?
opts: Take the dog for a walk
To try the plan for two weeks
To stop the dog going out

steps.en: I don't want to make a fuss, but it's rather difficult in the mornings.
steps.it: Non voglio fare storie, ma la mattina è piuttosto difficile.

steps.en: Shall we try it for two weeks and see how it goes?
steps.it: Proviamo per due settimane e vediamo come va?

steps.en: Sorry to bother you, but could I have a quick word?
steps.it: Scusa il disturbo, posso parlarti un momento?

lessons.title: Vicini di casa: lamentele cortesi
lessons.intro: In inglese una lamentela diretta suona aggressiva. Impari a dire le cose con garbo, a rispondere senza offendersi e a mettersi d'accordo.

steps.title: Lamentarsi con garbo
steps.body:
- **Sorry to bother you, but...** = Scusa il disturbo, ma...
- **Could I have a quick word?** = Posso parlarti un momento?
- **I don't want to make a fuss, but...** = Non voglio fare storie, ma...
- **Would you mind turning the music down?** (mind + -ing)
- **I was wondering if you could...** = Mi chiedevo se potresti...
- **It's just that...** = È solo che...

Da evitare: «You must stop the noise!» (ordine, scortese) e «I want that you...» (-> I'd like you to...).
ex: Would you mind keeping the noise down after eleven?
Ti dispiacerebbe fare meno rumore dopo le undici?
I was wondering if you could move your car.
Mi chiedevo se potresti spostare la macchina.

steps.title: Rispondere e trovare un accordo
steps.body:
Se sei tu a ricevere la lamentela:
- **I'm so sorry, I had no idea.** = Mi dispiace, non ne avevo idea.
- **I'll make sure it doesn't happen again.**
- **Thanks for letting me know.** = Grazie di avermelo detto.

Per accordarsi:
- **How about...?** / **Shall we try...?**
- **That sounds fair.** = Mi sembra giusto.
- **Let's see how it goes.** = Vediamo come va.
- **Do you want me to...?** = Vuoi che io...?

Per chiedere un favore: **Could you do me a favour?** / **Would you mind looking after my plants?**
ex: Thanks for letting me know. I'll keep it down.
Grazie di avermelo detto. Farò meno rumore.
Do you want me to bring in your post?
Vuoi che ritiri la tua posta?

steps.title: Il rumore della festa
steps.it: Scegli la battuta più naturale per te (Tu).

opts: Hi, sorry to bother you, but could I have a quick word?
Hi, I must to talk with you about your music.
Hello, you make too much noise, you must stop.
It's about the music last night. Would you mind turning it down after eleven?
It's about the music last night. I want that you turn down it after eleven.
It's about the music last night. Would you mind to turn down it after eleven?

lines: Oh, I'm so sorry. We had friends over. I'll make sure it doesn't happen again.

opts: Thanks, it's very pleasant for me.

steps.title: Un favore
steps.it: Il tuo vicino ti chiede aiuto. Scegli le risposte giuste.
lines: Hi! I wonder if you could do me a favour. Could you look after my plants while I'm away next week?

opts: Sure, no problem. How often should I water them?
Sure. How much times I have to water them?
Sure, no problem. How often I should water them?

lines: Twice a week is fine. Here's a spare key.

opts: Thanks. Do you want me to bring in your post as well?
Thanks. Do you want that I bring your post too?
Thanks. Want you that I take the post inside?

lines: That would be great. I'll bring you something back from Spain.

pairs: I don't want to make a fuss, but...
Would you mind keeping it down?

steps.it: Ti dispiacerebbe spostare la macchina?
steps.en: Would you mind moving your car
steps.why: Would you mind + -ing.

steps.en: I'm so sorry, I had no idea.
steps.it: Mi dispiace tanto, non ne avevo idea.

steps.en: Would you mind turning the music down?
steps.it: Ti dispiacerebbe abbassare la musica?
Vediamo come va.

steps.q: Your neighbour's dog barks every morning. Talk to your neighbour politely.
steps.it: Sei alla porta del vicino: introduci il problema con garbo, spiega perché ti disturba e proponi una soluzione (almeno 4 frasi).
steps.model: Hi, sorry to bother you, but could I have a quick word? It's about your dog. I don't want to make a fuss, but he barks every morning and I work from home. Would you mind leaving the radio on for him? Or how about trying a different time for his walk?

lessons.title: Scrivere un articolo
lessons.intro: Per il B1 Preliminary si scrive spesso un articolo per una rivista o un sito: titolo, apertura che cattura, opinione con esempi, chiusura con una domanda.

steps.title: Come è fatto un articolo
steps.body:
- **Titolo** chiaro, spesso una domanda: What makes a good neighbour?
- **Apertura** che coinvolge: Have you ever...? / Last year I...
- **Corpo**: opinione + esempi: In my opinion... / For example... / However...
- **Chiusura**: invito al lettore: Why not...? / What do you think?
- Tono semi-formale: poche contrazioni, niente slang.
- Usa varietà: phrasal verbs, forme in -ing, un paio di tempi diversi.

Errore tipico: scrivere tutto in un blocco o in elenco. Un articolo ha paragrafi brevi e connettivi: however, for example, as a result, in addition.
ex: In my opinion, a good neighbour respects your space.
Secondo me, un buon vicino rispetta i tuoi spazi.
Why not knock on their door and say hello?
Perché non bussare alla loro porta e salutare?

steps.s: Good neighbours say hello. ___ , they respect your privacy.
steps.why: Si aggiunge un'idea: in addition.

steps.s: I suggest ___ to your neighbours before you complain to anyone else.
steps.why: Suggest + -ing.

steps.s: I found out that my neighbour was growing up in Leeds.
answers: I found out that my neighbour had grown up in Leeds
I found out that my neighbour grew up in Leeds
steps.why: Si parla di un fatto passato concluso: grew up / had grown up.

steps.it: Perché non bussare alla loro porta?
steps.en: Why not knock on their door
steps.why: Why not + verbo base.

steps.q: Your college magazine is asking for articles called 'What makes a good neighbour?'. Write your article.
steps.it: Scrivi un articolo per la rivista con titolo «What makes a good neighbour?»: apertura personale, la tua opinione con almeno un esempio, un consiglio e una domanda finale per il lettore.
checklist: Ho scritto un titolo e diviso il testo in paragrafi
Ho espresso la mia opinione con In my opinion o I think
Ho dato almeno un esempio (For example...)
Ho usato almeno un phrasal verb (look after, put up with, find out...)
Ho usato almeno una forma in -ing dopo un verbo o una preposizione
Ho finito con una domanda al lettore
useful: look after / put up with / find out
steps.model:
What makes a good neighbour?

Last year I moved to a new street, and I soon found out that having good neighbours changes everything.

In my opinion, a good neighbour is someone who respects your space. They don't play loud music late at night, and they always say hello. However, a good neighbour also helps when you need it. For example, mine looked after my cat when I was away, and I took in her parcels.

Of course, nobody is perfect. If something bothers you, I suggest talking about it politely instead of complaining to other people.

Do you know your neighbours well? If not, why not knock on their door and introduce yourself?

steps.q: Describe your neighbours. Do you get on well with them?
steps.it: Parla dei tuoi vicini (o dei vicini ideali): come sono, se vi frequentate, un episodio.
steps.model: My neighbours are quite friendly. We usually say hello on the stairs, and sometimes we have a chat. Once, I locked myself out, and the woman next door let me wait in her flat. I'd like to know them better, but we're all very busy.

steps.q: Tell a story about a misunderstanding with a friend, a colleague or a neighbour.
steps.it: Racconta un malinteso: che cosa è successo, come vi siete chiariti, come è finita (usa i tempi del passato e fall out / make up).
steps.model: It all started when I forgot to reply to my friend's message. She thought I was angry with her, so she stopped calling me. After two weeks, I realised what had happened and I phoned her. We talked for an hour, we both apologised, and we made up.

lessons.title: Test dell'unità 10
lessons.intro: Verifica finale del livello B1: phrasal verbs, -ing / to, e ripasso di present perfect, tempi del passato, condizionali, passivo, discorso indiretto e relative.

steps.s: I ___ in this flat since 2019.
steps.why: Situazione che continua fino a oggi con since: present perfect.

steps.s: When I got to the station, the train ___ .
steps.why: Prima di un altro momento del passato: past perfect.

steps.s: If I ___ more money, I'd buy a bigger flat.
steps.why: Second conditional: if + past simple.

steps.s: This bridge ___ in 1890.
steps.why: Passivo al passato semplice con una data precisa.

steps.s: She said she ___ me the next day.
steps.why: Discorso indiretto: will diventa would.

steps.s: The woman ___ lives upstairs is a nurse.
steps.why: Per le persone, soggetto della relativa: who.

steps.s: Could you ___ the lights? I'm going to bed.
steps.why: Spegnere = turn off.

steps.q: Come dici «Ricordo di aver chiuso la porta a chiave»?
opts: I remember to lock the door.
steps.why: Un ricordo del passato: remember + -ing.
Forget + to per le azioni da fare.

opts: I can't put up with him.
I can't put up him with.
I can't put with up him.
steps.why: Il phrasal verb a tre parti non si separa.

steps.s: If I would have time, I would help you.
answers: If I had time, I would help you
If I had time, I'd help you
steps.why: Nella if-clause del second conditional si usa il past simple, non would.

steps.s: He said me that he was tired.
answers: He told me that he was tired
He said that he was tired
He told me he was tired
steps.why: Say non vuole il complemento di persona: told me / said that.

steps.s: I have seen her yesterday.
steps.why: Con yesterday serve il past simple.

steps.s: The film which I told you about it was great.
answers: The film which I told you about was great
The film I told you about was great
The film that I told you about was great
steps.why: Il pronome relativo sostituisce già «it»: non si ripete.

steps.s1: Someone stole my bike last night.
steps.why: Passivo del past simple: was + participio.

steps.s1: 'I will phone you tomorrow,' she said.
steps.s2: She said she ___ me the next day.
steps.why: Reported speech: will -> would.

steps.s1: The last time I saw him was in 2019.
steps.why: Since + present perfect: haven't seen.

steps.text: Ho smesso di fumare tre anni fa.
answers: I stopped smoking three years ago
I gave up smoking three years ago
I quit smoking three years ago
steps.why: Smettere di = stop + -ing; con «ago» serve il past simple.

steps.s: He sent me a long ___ for missing my birthday.
steps.why: Nome: apologise -> apology.

steps.s: We had a big ___ about the parking space and haven't spoken since.
steps.why: Argument = lite; topic e subject = argomento.

steps.s: They fell out last year, but they've ___ now.
steps.why: Make up = fare pace.

steps.it: Sono stati invitati alla festa.
steps.en: They were invited to the party
steps.why: Passivo: be + participio.

steps.title: Completa il testo
steps.text:
